goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — include_website_name` lacks the `?` suffix so AMS never calls it; website_name is always emitted (null when no website) instead of being omitted.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a conditional inclusion hook `def include_website_name` (no `?`) while adding `:website_name` to the serializer attributes list. In AMS/Discourse serializer conventions, conditional attribute hooks are typically `include_<attr>?`; without the `?` the hook won’t be invoked, so `website_name` would be serialized unconditionally (nil when `website` is blank) instead of being omitted as intended by `website.present?`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/user.js.es6:17 — Public controller property `websiteName` removed with no deprecation; themes/plugins that bind to `websiteName` break silently (no in-repo callers remain).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the controller computed property `websiteName` (user.js.es6) and updates the core template to use `model.website_name` instead, with no shim/deprecation path shown. While the claim about external themes/plugins breaking can’t be verified from this diff alone, the removal is real and represents a backwards-compatibility risk for any out-of-repo code that bound to `websiteName`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:43 — New `website_name` field is a display string whose format depends on server hostname, so API consumers get host-dependent values for the same website.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `website_name` to `UserSerializer` and computes it via `Discourse.current_hostname` in `website_name`, returning either just the host or `host + path` depending on whether the website domain matches/is parent of the instance domain. That means `json[:website_name]` for the same `website` can vary based on server hostname (as the new specs explicitly assert), which can be an API-stability/consumer expectation concern even if intended as a UI display string.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — include_website_name` lacks the `?` suffix so AMS never uses it as an include filter; the method is dead code and website_name is always serialized

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb` the conditional include hook is defined as `def include_website_name` (no `?`). In ActiveModel::Serializer/Discourse serializer conventions, conditional attribute hooks are typically `include_<attr>?`; with the current name the hook is unlikely to be invoked, so `:website_name` (added to the serialized attributes list) would be serialized unconditionally (potentially as `null`) instead of being gated by `website.present?` as intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:145 — Sibling check compares every label after the first, so unrelated hosts under a shared public suffix (e.g. evil.co.uk vs forum.co.uk, a.github.io vs b.github.io) are treated as the same domain and the full path is shown

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name` the “sibling subdomain” branch triggers when `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` and length > 2, then compares everything except the first label (`split('.')[1..-1]`). This will treat hosts like `a.github.io` vs `b.github.io` (both end in `github.io`) or `evil.co.uk` vs `forum.co.uk` (both end in `co.uk`) as the “same domain” and return `website_host + URI(...).path`, exposing the full path when it shouldn’t. That behavior follows directly from the diff logic at the cited area.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:148 — Only matches when the website is the parent of the instance host, so www.example.com on an example.com instance (or deeper subdomains of different length) shows only the host, which is inconsistent with the stated intent

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, the logic includes the path only when `website_host == discourse_host`, when both hosts have the same dot-segment length and share the same parent domain (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`), or when the instance host ends with `"." + website_host` (website is a parent of the instance, e.g. `example.com` vs `forums.example.com`). It does *not* include the path when the website is a subdomain of the instance host (e.g. `website_host=www.example.com`, `discourse_host=example.com`) or when subdomain depths differ, so those cases fall through to returning only `website_host`. This is a diff-grounded edge-case gap in the newly added nontrivial host-matching logic, though the finding’s phrasing "only matches when the website is the parent" is not strictly accurate because the equal-length sibling-subdomain branch also matches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:138 — Websites saved without a scheme (e.g. "example.com") parse with a nil host, so website_name is nil and the website line is hidden completely even though a website is set

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the template now renders the website row only when `model.website_name` is truthy (`{{#if model.website_name}}`), not when `model.website` is present. The serializer’s `include_website_name` returns true whenever `website.present?`, but `website_name` itself returns nil when `URI(website.to_s).host` is nil. For schemeless values like `"example.com"`, Ruby’s `URI(...)` yields a nil host, so `website_name` becomes nil and the UI hides the website despite `website` being set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:148 — "." << website_host` mutates a string literal; this raises FrozenError if frozen string literals are enabled (use "." + website_host)

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, the expression `"." << website_host` does use `<<` to mutate the receiver string literal (`"."`). This is safe in normal Ruby (since the literal isn’t frozen by default), but it will raise `FrozenError` if frozen string literals are enabled (via magic comment or global setting). The diff doesn’t show frozen string literals being enabled, so it’s not a verifiable current bug, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded robustness/compat issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:141 — Host comparisons are case-sensitive and ignore a trailing dot or port, so hosts that differ only in case do not match

adjudication.rationale: The new `website_name` logic compares `website_host` and `discourse_host` using plain string equality / `ends_with?` (e.g., `website_host == discourse_host`, `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`), with no explicit normalization of `discourse_host` (lowercasing, stripping trailing dot). Ruby string comparisons are case-sensitive, so if `Discourse.current_hostname` were not normalized (or had a trailing dot), hosts differing only by case/trailing dot would not match and the path-including behavior would not trigger. The diff does not show `current_hostname`’s normalization, so this is a specific edge-case concern created by the change, but not a clearly reproducible defect from the diff alone. Also, the claim about ports is not clearly supported here because `URI(...).host` drops the port.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:43 — website_name is added as a plain attribute outside untrusted_attributes and its guard `include_website_name` lacks the `?` so it never runs, leaking TL0 users' website host/path to anonymous viewers and bypassing restrict_user_fields?

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `:website_name` is added inside the `untrusted_attributes` list (alongside `:website`), not “outside” it. Also, while the serializer defines `def include_website_name` without a trailing `?` (which may mean the usual `include_...?(...)` hook won’t be invoked, depending on the serializer framework), the claimed security impact (“never runs, leaking TL0 users’ website host/path to anonymous viewers and bypassing restrict_user_fields”) is not verifiable from this diff alone and is overstated given `website_name` is explicitly marked untrusted here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:146 — Same-domain check compares naive label suffixes (e.g. forum.example.co.uk vs evil.example.co.uk, or example.co.uk vs evil.co.uk) so unrelated attacker domains get the "trusted" full-path display

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, the branch `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` treats two hosts as “same site” if they match after dropping the first label: `website_host.split('.')[1..-1] == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1]`. This is incorrect for multi-label public suffixes like `co.uk`: `example.co.uk` and `evil.co.uk` both become `co.uk`, so the code will return `website_host + path` for an unrelated domain, which matches the finding’s “naive label suffix” concern and changes behavior to display the full path for an external site.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:149 — ends_with?("." + website_host) treats bare TLD/public-suffix hosts (e.g. http://com/login) as parents of the instance domain, showing attacker-chosen paths as if same-site

adjudication.rationale: The new `website_name` logic in `user_serializer.rb` treats any `website_host` as a potential “parent” domain of the instance via `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host) ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host`. For a host like `com` (e.g. `http://com/login`, where `URI(...).host` can be `"com"`), an instance hostname like `example.com` will satisfy `ends_with?(".com")` and the code will return `"com/login"`, incorrectly appending the path as if it were same-site/parent-related. This is a real edge-case defect introduced by the diff (no public-suffix/TLD guarding).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/user.hbs:66 — Showing the full user-controlled path as link text on same-domain URLs (e.g. /admin or /session/login-looking paths) makes misleading in-forum-looking links easier for phishing

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the displayed website link text from host-only (removed `websiteName` in `user.js.es6`) to `model.website_name` (template `user.hbs`), and the new serializer method `website_name` explicitly returns `website_host + path` when the website host equals the instance host or is a parent domain (e.g., `example.com/user`). This means a user-controlled website like `http://example.com/admin` on an `example.com` instance will render link text `example.com/admin`, making it easier to present an in-forum-looking path as the visible label. This is a security/UX regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:144 — Sibling-subdomain branch (www.example.com vs forum.example.com) and its mismatch case (www.other.com vs forum.example.com) have no test coverage despite the code comment claiming support.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial branching logic in `UserSerializer#website_name`, including an explicit sibling-subdomain case (`elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2`) intended to handle scenarios like `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`, with both a match and a mismatch path. The added spec covers: different domains (`discourse.org` vs `example.com`), exact same domain (`example.com`), and parent-domain relationship (`forums.example.com` with `example.com`). It does not cover the sibling-subdomain branch at all (e.g., `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) nor its mismatch case (e.g., `www.other.com` vs `forum.example.com`), so the finding about missing coverage is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:153 — include_website_name lacks the trailing '?' so it is never used as a filter, and no test checks that website_name is omitted for a blank or nil website.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `website_name` plus a conditional method `include_website_name`, but Discourse/AMS conditional attribute inclusion relies on the `include_<attr>?` naming convention. Because the method is missing the trailing `?`, it won’t be used to filter the `website_name` attribute, so `website_name` may be serialized even when `website` is blank (likely as `null`). The added specs only cover non-empty websites and don’t assert omission when website is blank/nil.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:138 — No tests cover a nil/blank website, an invalid URI (the rescue path), or a website with no scheme (e.g. 'example.com' yields nil host and no website shown).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial `website_name` logic in `user_serializer.rb` that explicitly handles failure via `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` and returns early if the host is nil. The added spec only covers valid `http://example.com/user` cases with different `Discourse.current_hostname` values; it does not cover blank/nil `website`, invalid URIs hitting the `rescue`, or inputs without a scheme (e.g. `example.com` where `URI(...).host` is nil). This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in test coverage for newly introduced branches.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:149 — No test for a website subdomain with an apex instance (www.example.com vs example.com) or a lookalike suffix (badexample.com vs forum.example.com), which the ends_with? check is meant to reject.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial domain-comparison logic in `UserSerializer#website_name`, including an `ends_with?("." << website_host)` branch intended to distinguish parent-domain relationships from lookalike suffixes. The added specs cover different domains, exact match, and instance subdomain vs website apex (`forums.example.com` vs `example.com`), but they do not cover the inverse (website subdomain vs apex instance like `www.example.com` vs `example.com`) nor a lookalike suffix case (e.g., `badexample.com` vs `forum.example.com`) to validate the suffix rejection behavior. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap rather than a demonstrated defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:87 — Tests only use a website with a path; none checks a root URL ('http://example.com' gives 'example.com/' with a trailing slash) or that query/fragment are dropped.

adjudication.rationale: The updated specs set `user.user_profile.website = 'http://example.com/user'` and only assert `website_name` for that path-bearing URL. The new serializer logic in `UserSerializer#website_name` builds output from `URI(...).host` and sometimes appends `URI(...).path`, but there are no tests for a root URL with an empty/`/` path (e.g. `'http://example.com'`) nor for URLs containing query/fragment to confirm they’re intentionally excluded. This is a concrete gap in coverage for the newly added nontrivial behavior, not a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/user.hbs:66 — The template switch from the websiteName controller property to model.website_name, and the removal of that property, has no JS/QUnit or acceptance test for the rendered profile link.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the controller computed property `websiteName` and updates the template to render `model.website_name` instead (user.hbs). While Ruby serializer specs were added to cover `website_name` JSON behavior, this diff does not add any front-end (QUnit/acceptance) test that verifies the profile page renders the website link text/URL correctly using `model.website_name`, so UI-level coverage for this behavioral change is missing in the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:78 — Tests stub Discourse.current_hostname instead of setting the real hostname/base URL, so the comparison against the real instance host is not exercised.

adjudication.rationale: The spec explicitly stubs `Discourse.current_hostname` in each example (e.g., `Discourse.stubs(:current_hostname).returns('discourse.org')`) to exercise the branching in `UserSerializer#website_name`. That’s a normal/unit-test approach for code that depends on environment state; the diff does not show any “real hostname/base URL” mechanism that should be set instead, nor does it show a failure to test the serializer logic itself.
